summary: An FP8 E4M3 KV cache with one scale per position and key/value head, read by flash-style prompt attention and by decode attention whose launch and work do not depend on the cache's capacity
implementation_scope: CUDA source for head dimensions 64, 128 and 256: a write kernel quantizing chunk rows per head vector; causal prompt attention with 128-query blocks, register prefetch of the next FP8 tile, BF16 dequantization into a swizzled shared stage, BF16 tensor cores and an online softmax; an opt-in prompt attention on E4M3 tensor cores (E4M3 queries, cache codes as stored, value scales folded into E4M3 probabilities, 64-key cp.async tiles); decode attention over a fixed grid of blocks per key/value head merging strided 128-key pieces, with a fixed-order combine, device-side positions for graph capture and column invariance; a host model of the encoding. Paged caches, projections and rotary embedding are engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: The KV cache limits the context that fits on the device, decode at long context is bound by cache reads, or the engine must serve a required context without becoming slower for short requests
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The cache is small next to the weights at the target context, the cache is paged or shared across requests without adapted loads, or the model needs finer than per-head-vector scales
provides: E4M3 codes with one FP32 scale per position and key/value head (max |x| / 448), written per chunk
Register prefetch of the next FP8 tile and BF16 dequantization into one swizzled shared K / V stage
Causal grouped-query prompt attention with 128 queries per block, tile skipping after a warp's last query and heaviest tiles first
prefill_fp8: the same prompt attention with Q K^T and P V on E4M3 mma.m16n8k32, for engines whose quality budget allows E4M3 probabilities
Decode attention over a fixed grid whose launch and work depend only on the tokens held, with the position read from device memory
Column invariance: a column decoded alone equals the same column inside a multi-column verify, bit for bit
A host model of the encoding and of the values the kernels read
engine_supplies: Keys after normalization and rotary embedding, written before the attention that reads them
Queries in BF16 and the output gate or projection after attention
The capacity, the blocks per key/value head and the partial buffer
Whole-model quality measurement of FP8 storage against its quality budget
preserve: In prefill and decode, one scale per head vector, applied when the tile is dequantized, never folded into rounded probabilities (prefill_fp8 folds the value scale into its E4M3 probabilities by design)
A fully masked tile leaves a row's maximum, sum and output unchanged
Piece-to-block assignment and combine order that depend only on key positions, so results depend only on a column's position
Decode work that grows with the tokens held, not with the capacity
adapt: Tile, piece and block sizes, rows per decode block and supported head dimensions
Scale granularity and format (per group of dimensions, FP16 scales)
Paged cache loads and sharing a dequantized tile across more query heads

code_files.purpose: Cache layout and the write, prefill and decode interfaces
Write, prompt attention (BF16 and E4M3 tensor cores), decode attention and combine kernels for head dimensions 64, 128 and 256
Host E4M3 encoding with per-head scales and the dequantized values the kernels read

requires.hardware: CUDA C++17+ on sm_89+ (E4M3 conversions, BF16 mma.sync, ldmatrix, cp.async); Python 3.11+ standard library for the reference
requires.model: Softmax attention with grouped-query (or multi-head) key/value heads, head dimension 64, 128 or 256
requires.workload: Long contexts and single-request decode or speculative verify with up to 64 rows (columns times query heads per key/value head)

contract.input: BF16 key and value rows for write; BF16 queries [T][q_stride], the cache, T, the position (host or device), head counts and score scale for attention
contract.output: FP8 codes and FP32 scales in the cache; FP32 attention output [T][out_stride] per query head
contract.ownership: The engine owns queries, cache, scratch and output; launches borrow them on the caller stream
contract.failure: Null buffers, non-positive sizes, heads not a multiple of key/value heads, unaligned or short strides, unsupported head dimensions, more than 64 decode rows or a block count outside 1..1024 return cudaErrorInvalidValue; launch errors are returned
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; the kernels run inside the engine's forward passes

dependencies: CUDA runtime with cuda_bf16.h and cuda_fp8.h
Python standard library for the reference

validation.host: E4M3 codes round-trip, saturate at 448 and dequantize within E4M3 precision; all-zero vectors take scale 1
validation.native: Head dimensions 64/128/256, grouped and ungrouped heads, later chunks and multi-piece decode against FP64 softmax over the dequantized cache: at most 1.5e-3 of the output magnitude on sm_120; each decode column alone bit for bit equal to the multi-column result; prefill_fp8 on the same cases within 7.3e-2 of the output magnitude (E4M3 queries and probabilities)
validation.performance: One measured engine (head dimension 256, 24 query and 4 key/value heads, RTX 5090): the context that fits rose from about 122K to 244,736 tokens, and an engine opened at a quarter of that capacity ran within 1% of the full one. prefill_fp8 vs prefill on that GPU, 4,096 queries: 73.1 -> 35.7 ms over 131K keys at head dimension 256 (24/4 heads), 54.9 -> 29.7 ms at 128 (32/4 heads); in that engine (Qwen3.8-27B) prefill quality went from 16.7% to 18.8% of the drift budget and long-context first token from 18.5 s to 15.9 s (geometric mean); no claim for other shapes
